headline: Sleep debt is today's story — protect it; the hard work (Un1t) is already banked, so hold everything else easy.
body_state: Readiness sits at 52 (composite 61.5, moderate band) with **sleep** as the driver: 26h of debt built up over the last 14 days and last night gave you only 6.3h (sleep score 66, 22 restless moments). HRV is rebounding — 45ms and BALANCED, up from 38ms yesterday — and body battery started at 47 after a strong +44 overnight recharge. Garmin still reads Recovery status. TSB is -10.5, squarely in the -5 to -30 productive-training band, so the fatigue itself isn't a red flag — the sleep debt underneath it is.
session: No plan run today — Base week 1 of the new Half Marathon plan (target 90:00, 2026-09-21) has nothing scheduled until tomorrow. This morning's Un1t class is already done: 46 min, RPE 7, 53% of the time in zone 4, and HR was still climbing at the finish — no cooldown. That's a genuinely hard session on a moderate-readiness morning, so treat the rest of today as recovery. Tomorrow brings the block's first quality day: 4km tempo at 4:18-4:32/km bracketed by 10-min easy legs at 4:50-5:19/km — hold those legs genuinely easy, not the 4:20s you've been calling 'easy' lately.
recent: The pattern this week is grey-zone training. Aug 7's 'easy' progressive long run closed at 179bpm/RPE 8 and readiness crashed to 23 the next day. Aug 10's '5km Easy Run' ran 4:27/km with 89.7% of time in zone 3, not zone 1-2. Today's Un1t repeated the shape at 53% Z4. `ranked_limiters` confirms it: only 17.8% of running time is true easy vs an ~80% target. Aug 8's Un1t was the one clean green match in this stretch (42min, HR 130). Nothing here is dangerous in isolation, but it's why readiness keeps whiplashing instead of climbing.
focus: Bedtime ~60min earlier for the next two weeks — 26h of sleep debt is today's real constraint
Tomorrow's tempo: hold the 10-min warm-up/cooldown at genuinely easy pace (4:50-5:19/km), not the 4:20s you've drifted to
Grey-zone training is limiter #1 (17.8% easy vs 80% target) — every 'easy' label needs to actually be easy, starting tomorrow
